analysis.investment_thesis: Data Patterns is a high-quality defence electronics business — zero debt, excellent margins at 43%, strong growth — but at 79x trailing P/E and 60x EV/EBITDA on a company earning INR 222 Cr of profit, this is a speculation on India's defence spending, not an investment. I do not pay 79x earnings for any business.
key_strengths: Pristine balance sheet — zero debt, and the business has never needed leverage to grow
Exceptional operating margins at 43% reflect genuine technological differentiation in defence electronics
Revenue CAGR of 31.6% over 3 years with net profit compounding at 33.1% — the growth is real and accelerating
key_risks: Valuation at 79x trailing P/E, P/B of 12.72x, and P/S of 20x prices in a decade of perfect execution — any project delay or order miss destroys this valuation
Operating cash flow was negative INR 90 Cr in FY25 and negative INR 17 Cr in FY23 — a profitable business converting less than half its years to positive OCF has serious working capital issues
Defence procurement is entirely dependent on government budget allocation and approval cycles — revenue is lumpy, not predictable
red_flags: Free cash flow was negative INR 196 Cr in FY25 — the company's reported profits are not translating into cash, which is a fundamental quality concern
OCF positive in only 2 of 4 years — for a business I'm being asked to pay 79x earnings, this cash conversion problem is unacceptable
Promoter holding at 42.41% is adequate but the overall float and institutional holding are still thin; price can be extremely volatile on any negative news
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I have no objection to the underlying business — defence electronics is a genuinely strategic industry with strong barriers, and Data Patterns has demonstrated it can win complex contracts with excellent margins. But my job as an investor is not to find good businesses; it is to find good businesses at prices that protect my capital. At INR 19,562 Cr market cap for a business that earned INR 222 Cr of net profit in FY25, I am paying 88 years of earnings at current levels. Even if profits double again, the stock is still expensive.

The working capital problem is the other issue I cannot overlook. Defence customers — particularly DRDO and Indian armed forces — are notoriously slow payers. This creates a structural mismatch between profit recognition and cash receipt. Two of four years with negative operating cash flow, and negative free cash flow of INR 196 Cr in FY25, means the 'profits' are partly sitting in receivables. I have seen many defence and infrastructure companies look profitable on paper and struggle for cash. Avoid at this price.
